name: The Chicago Democrat

partners.name: John Calhoun
partners.basis: The register matches the printed name to the town card calhoun_john (action: enrich), so this is the same person the resident layer already holds. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

partners.name: Calhoun, J.
partners.basis: A proprietor string the gazetteer reads as a person, which the register's own person list does not carry under this spelling. The name is the evidence; no link is claimed. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

locations.basis: Placeable against the committed town. A crossing of two platted streets: clark and south_water.
locations.limit_reason: The register places this house against clark+south_water and the town holds no roof of its own for it (action: new_building), so the anchor is as far as the reading goes.

anchor.title: Clark Street and South Water Street

locations.basis: The later of this house's two printed anchors, set as “Jones & King's hardware store”; the register makes “the corner of South Water and Clark streets” the siting at the scene date.
locations.limit_reason: A prose anchor the register did not resolve to a committed id; kept because the house moved and the move is dated. First printed 1835-08-05, which is after the scene date, so the register keeps the earlier anchor live and this siting is recorded without being made the premises.

dates.basis: No opening is announced. The first printing, 1833-11-26, is the bound: the house was trading by then and the record does not say when it began.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read yankee: John Calhoun (yankee). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A directory, a deed or a later reading that names this house's premises, its staff or its dates more exactly than the newspapers do.
